title: Groter, groter, het grootst
summary: Comparatives (groter dan), superlatives (het grootst / de grootste) and the key irregulars

blocks.title: Vergroten: -er + dan
blocks.body: To compare, add **-er** to the adjective and link with **dan** (than). *groot → groter*, *klein → kleiner*. *Amsterdam is groter dan Utrecht.* Adjectives ending in **-r** add **-der** for sound: *duur → duurder*, *lekker → lekkerder*.
blocks.callout: Watch spelling: *groot* has a double-o, but *groter* drops one (open syllable stays long).

blocks.title: Het meest: -st
blocks.body: For the top of the scale, add **-st**. Two shapes: standing alone use **het …st** (*In juli is het het warmst*), and in front of a noun use **de/het …ste** (*de grootste stad*). Even *duur* just adds -st: *het duurst*.

items.target: In de winter is het het koudst.
items.speak: In de winter is het het koudst.

blocks.title: De onregelmatige drie
blocks.body: Three very common words don't follow the pattern — learn them as a set, exactly like English good/better/best.
blocks.callout: *graag/liever/liefst* is how you rank preferences: *Ik drink graag koffie, maar liever thee, en het liefst chocomel.*

pairs.note: *liever* = 'rather' (prefer one over another). *het liefst* = 'most of all' (your absolute favourite).

options: Deze fiets is goeder dan die.
Deze fiets is beter dan die.
Deze fiets is meer goed dan die.

blocks.prompt: Say 'Tea is tastier than coffee.' (thee, koffie, lekker)
blocks.hint: lekker ends in -r → add -der. Link with dan.
blocks.explain: *Thee is lekkerder dan koffie.* — the -r adjective takes -der.

blocks.title: Maak een vergelijking
blocks.prompt: Compare two things with a comparative + dan.
blocks.sample: Deze trein is sneller dan de bus.

blocks.scene: Daan defends the smaller cities over a beer

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.target: Amsterdam is leuk, maar Utrecht is gezelliger, vind ik.
lines.en: Amsterdam is nice, but Utrecht is cosier, I think.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Echt? Amsterdam is toch veel groter en drukker.
lines.en: Really? Amsterdam is much bigger and busier though.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.target: Precies. Klein is beter. En het bier is er goedkoper, hoor.
lines.en: Exactly. Small is better. And the beer's cheaper there, you know.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Haha, dát is jouw beste argument.
lines.spotlight: beste — superlative of goed, before a noun.

questions.q: Why does Daan prefer Utrecht, in the end?
options: It's cosier and the beer is cheaper

blocks.prompt: Compare your old town and your new one: write two sentences with a comparative + *dan*, and one with *het liefst* (what you like most of all).
